clue.text: One likes to shoot heroin that's pure under small needle

indicators.note: in a down answer, the heroin and purity pieces sit under the small piece, so they follow it

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
H is slang shorthand for heroin
utter means pure or absolute, as in utter nonsense
to needle someone is to bug or annoy them

explanation.surface: A grim picture of a drug user wanting to inject unadulterated heroin with a tiny needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' and 'needle' paint a drug scene, but the shooting is with a camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutterbug is an enthusiastic amateur photographer, someone who loves taking shots with a camera.

clue.text: They lie over large cushions

indicators.note: the cushioning word is laid over the large abbreviation, covering it and so holding it within

parts.note: buffers cushion an impact, as on railway stops

explanation.surface: People lounging on top of big pillows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' suggests reclining on the cushions; it means telling untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluffers are deceivers who pretend to hold strength they lack, so they are people telling untruths.

clue.text: Getting up one's nose

parts.note: the word one gives the article A; the apostrophe-s is a link meaning 'is'
a wine's nose is its scent or aroma

explanation.surface: Something getting up your nose, like an irritation or a sniff of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting up, as in rising or climbing, is the act of going upward: a climb.

clue.text: Bit of love during sex that's ace

indicators.note: the love letter falls during, i.e. inside, the word for sex

parts.note: IT is a coy old word for sex or sex appeal
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
A is the abbreviation for ace in playing cards

explanation.surface: Someone praising a little romance during an excellent sexual encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount or jot is a bit; the Greek letter's name is used for the smallest quantity.

clue.text: This man will party?

parts.note: this man will contracts to he'll, written without its apostrophe
a bender is a drinking spree, a wild party

explanation.surface: A question about whether some man is going to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: the whole clue describes a reckless reveller. Some solvers felt a bender is a binge rather than a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hellbender is a dissolute person given to wild, reckless revelry; it is also an American giant salamander.

clue.text: Lined up a college to return to adult world of learning

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: returning sends the word for lined up back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: to have lined up a shot is to have aimed it

explanation.surface: A student queueing to go back to a college, entering the grown-up world of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lined up' suggests queueing but means aimed. The piece 'to return' works on comes first in the clue yet ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the community and environment of universities, scholarship and research: the scholarly realm.

clue.text: School tackling sport and English language

indicators.note: the school abbreviation tackles, i.e. grips round, the sport and English letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school sport

explanation.surface: A school timetable combining games with English lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech is spoken language, the faculty of expressing thoughts in words.

clue.text: Flyers go up

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the word for go is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to have a go is to have a stab at something

explanation.surface: Pilots or aircraft taking off into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats are the only mammals capable of true flight, so they are winged creatures that take to the air.

clue.text: My good cure

parts.note: holy means good in the saintly, virtuous sense
to cure fish or meat is to preserve it, for example by smoking it

explanation.surface: Someone proudly calling a remedy their own, or a doctor praising their treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive; it is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of astonishment, interchangeable as cries of 'Well, I never!'

clue.text: Caught up with secretary for tea?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written
a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: An office scene: catching up with a colleague over a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is informal British slang for a cup of tea, the classic office break drink.

clue.text: Fabric is fine to iron later around the edges

indicators.note: the farewell word sits around the edges of the fine and iron letters, enclosing them

parts.note: later and ta-ta are both casual ways of saying goodbye
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
FE is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Laundry advice: a fabric is fine, but iron its edges later.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, smooth woven fabric, typically silk, used for dresses and linings.

clue.text: Open supermarket close to village with empty shops

parts.note: Lidl is a discount supermarket chain

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of village
empty shops is the word shops with its inside removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A discount store opens near a village whose high street has emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like opening a store; it describes an eye with no lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking eyelids means eyes cannot be closed, so they remain permanently uncovered and staring.

clue.text: Still time to make meeting

parts.note: still and even both intensify a comparison: still better, even better

explanation.surface: There is still time to make it to the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports meeting is a gathering or fixture of competitions, as in an athletics occasion.

clue.text: Crew is behind section in vessel

indicators.note: the crew piece comes behind, after, the section letter

parts.note: crew is gives team's, written without its apostrophe
in and hip both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A ship's crew placed behind one section of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a ship driven by steam engines, one kind of seagoing craft.

clue.text: Dressing a boy in top for Sunday best

indicators.note: the article and boy go inside the top letter and best word combined
top for means the opening letter of Sunday

parts.note: the cream is the best of anything, as in cream of the crop
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A young lad in his finest top, dressed in Sunday best for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' and 'Sunday best' suggest clothes; it is a sauce for salads.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a tangy, mayonnaise-like sauce poured over salads, a British condiment.

clue.text: Nit-pickings of a president that's terrible

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of a president are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about the petty quibbles of an awful head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is fussy insistence on minor details and rules; pedantries are instances of that fussiness.

clue.text: Pitches on this ground, getting delivery that's hard

parts.note: the ground or basis of something is its base
in cricket each delivery by the bowler is a ball
diamond is the hardest natural substance

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a bowler sending down a tough delivery on this pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitches' and 'delivery' point to cricket; the pitching is done by baseball pitchers.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the pitcher throws from the mound at the centre of the infield, the square named for its gem-like shape.

clue.text: Poor wine settled

parts.note: broke means poor, having no money
red is wine, as in a glass of red

explanation.surface: A cheap wine that has settled in the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To broker a deal is to arrange or negotiate it, so a brokered dispute is one that has been resolved.

clue.text: Flavour of plain drink

parts.note: overt means plain, open to view
one is a drink, as in fancy one at the pub?

explanation.surface: A wine taster noting the taste of a simple drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertone or suggestion, as in a remark with overtones of menace, is a flavour or hint of something.

clue.text: Rod might drink daughter's tea

parts.note: rod is gangster slang for a gun

indicators.note: the might word drinks, i.e. takes in, the daughter letter

parts.note: might means power or strength
D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Rod, a man's name, might be drinking his daughter's cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' reads as a man's name but is the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder is a Chinese green tea whose leaves are rolled into small pellets resembling shot.

clue.text: As good as new in the morning

parts.note: early means in the morning, as in early hours

explanation.surface: Something looking as good as new first thing in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: As good as and almost both mean all but, as in 'as good as finished'.

clue.text: Polish mum once called round

parts.note: mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence

indicators.note: round signals turning the word for once called back to front

parts.note: née, French for born, introduces a woman's former name, i.e. what she was once called

explanation.surface: A Polish mother who used to come round to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to look like the nationality; it means shine. 'once called' is the maiden-name marker née, and 'round' turns it about.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheen is a gloss or lustre on a surface, the shine that polishing produces.

clue.text: Mark King's cracking melody

indicators.note: the king's letter is cracking, i.e. breaking into, the word for mark

parts.note: a stain is a mark
R is the abbreviation for king, from the Latin rex

explanation.surface: Mark King, a musician, playing an excellent tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark King' reads as a person's name; Mark is the stain and King gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of music or a tune, as in the strains of a violin.

clue.text: American friend, turning over sport, getting armchair

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: turning over flips the sport abbreviation so it is read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a sport

explanation.surface: An American pal switching the TV channel to sport from his armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' suggests changing channel; it reverses RU to UR.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic or fan is one without professional experience: a non-professional.

clue.text: Prodigal son covers up further

indicators.note: the words prodigal son cover up the answer, concealing it within their letters

explanation.surface: The wasteful son in the parable hides something further.
explanation.definitionFit: Further and in addition both mean besides, adding another point.

clue.text: Keeper of dog for men

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
at can mean for, as in sold at or for a pound
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A kennel keeper looking after a dog on behalf of some men.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum or gallery official in charge of the collection is its keeper, a British title for that post.

clue.text: See old cover for Playboy issue

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced like see, so it can stand for it

indicators.note: the cover of the word Playboy is its outer letters

explanation.surface: Look at a vintage magazine cover for a Playboy edition.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a magazine is a single copy or edition of it.

clue.text: Figure out one divided by five

indicators.note: the single word is divided, split open, by the five numeral

parts.note: sole means single, only one
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An arithmetic sum: work out one divided by five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided by' looks like arithmetic; it means V splits SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure out a problem is to work out its answer, to crack it.

clue.text: IT company: one can supply parts for device

indicators.note: the company name parts, splitting open to hold the other letters

parts.note: Apple is a computer technology company
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: read as supplely, i.e. nimbly bent, it signals rearranging the letters of can

explanation.surface: A tech firm saying one can buy spare components for its gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' reads as provide but is the adverb of supple, rearranging CAN to ANC.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a machine or gadget designed for a household task, such as a toaster.
